newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban union calls for revival of sugar sector.
newsitem.headline: Cuban union calls for revival of sugar sector.

text.p: Cuba's umbrella labor union called Monday for a revival of the island's depressed sugar sector, saying this year's harvest had not been satisfactory.

The appeal was made in an editorial in the weekly trade union newspaper Trabajadores. The paper reiterated predictions made earlier this month by President Fidel Castro that the nearly-completed 1996-97 sugar cane harvest would not, as previously hoped, be an improvement on last year's harvest.

Authorities on the communist-ruled island had originally expected what they called a modest increase over 1995-96 production of 4.45 million tonnes. That harvest, while still low by traditional Cuban standards, marked the end of a disastrous five-year slump in the sector.
Officials have not yet issued any estimated production figure for the current harvest, due to end in the coming weeks.

But Trabajadores said this year's harvest would leave a "shadow of dissatisfaction", even if there had been unavoidable difficulties such as a hurricane in October that damaged some cane before the start of the harvest in December, and delays in the arrival of foreign financing for technical input to the crop.

The newspaper said the main problem for the harvest had been an insufficient quantity of cane, but also added that some mills had production costs that were far too high. There was a possibility that in the future mills that were inefficient might have to be closed down, the paper added.

It noted that meeting this year's target of sowing of some 890,000 acres (360,000 hectares) of new cane was vital to ensuring an improved harvest next year, as was getting on with the task of weeding cane.
